threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line' and ask for the 'quickest route' instead of embracing the chaos.
Last night on the 35, a guy argued with his reflection in the window for a solid 20 minutes. Brixton at midnight, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the neighbor's parrot started mimicking the U-Bahn announcements—perfectly. That was my wake-up call.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find currywurst stalls that open at 6 AM, serving drunchies to night owls and early risers alike. It's a local rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're a local when you navigate the BART delays like a pro, but still refuse to touch Muni after they left you waiting with a dog on the tracks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a full Muni car stop to let a raccoon wander across the street. The passengers didn’t bat an eye. Just another day in the city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is only about fancy cafés; they miss the local bakeries where the real morning magic happens. Fresh pa de pessic is a must.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their still-fresh appreciation for the magic of the light bouncing off the buildings at sunset—like they’ve never seen anything quite like it.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston Junction is where you catch the train, instead of just a good spot for brunch and vintage shops.
Last night on the 36, a guy serenaded the bus with an old soul tune. Everyone joined in—never thought Peckham could feel so together at 2 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy juggling in the Park am Gleisdreieck while a child tried to catch pigeons with a homemade net.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous dance battle at a bus stop, where onlookers cheer more than at a club. It's a vibe you can't replicate.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local when they know that the green light at 16th and Mission means you better hustle or risk being stuck in a crowd.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy juggling oranges on the 31 Balboa this morning. Distracted everyone from the usual crowded silence—just another San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think the plaça is just for photos, but locals use it for Sunday chess and spontaneous concerts, not just a backdrop.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their puzzled look at the metro map; locals just hop on without a second glance.
